_about: Journeys page data (site/journeys.qmd). Edit this file, then run: python3 scripts/build_journeys.py (writes _journeys.qmd) and re-render.
Source of every fact: Henry's own account (2026-11-05) and his route images. Public text is English, one line per entry.
home: the place id of Henry's hometown (its province's tile says 'home' instead of a first-visit year).
chapters: one per place lived, in time order; colour = [day, night] (validated as a categorical set for adjacent chapters).

places: id -> name, admin (ISO 3166-2 style: CN-xx for China's provincial-level divisions, US-xx for U.S. states and DC), country (ISO alpha-2; HK for Hong Kong as a region), lat/lon (approximate city centres).

entries: date (YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD where the day is shown), optional end and when (the date words shown), chapter, text, places (the stops this entry claims: dots on the map), optional parent (a stop of a longer journey), transit (place ids landed at between flights) and noentry (transits without entering the country), first (list of 'first' badges), milestone (badge words), route or routes.

route: mode ground (by road or rail), flight, or unknown (way of travel not recorded); path = place ids and '@lat,lon' shaping points (shaping points make no claim of a visit; every mapped route is approximate); passes = provincial divisions or states passed through (they light the tiles); km = a distance Henry gave (otherwise the length of the drawn line is used).
draft: a short note on what was inferred; on an entry, a place, or a pass (a code ending in '?'). Henry confirms or corrects these; the build lists them.

entries.text: Left home in Shouguang, Shandong, for university in Baotou: my first time away from home, and the farthest I had been.
Ordos and Hohhot, many times: both are close to Baotou.
Yinchuan, Ningxia, over the May Day holiday: my first real trip that was not for school.
Datong, Shanxi: climbed Mount Heng, the North of the Five Great Mountains and my first of the five.
first: First of the Five Great Mountains

entries.text: Qingdao, for the first time, in the summer holiday.
Cycled from Baotou to the Kubuqi Desert: my first desert.
Sixty days around China in the summer holiday: 17 provinces and regions, 33 cities and 12,162 km, and the last of the Five Great Mountains, all climbed and descended on foot.

route.note: The 17 provinces and regions are the ones named on the 2013 map; the line between the named stops is drawn from that map.

entries.text: Xi'an: Mount Hua (the West), the Qinling, the Terracotta Army, Datang Everbright City and the Big Wild Goose Pagoda.
Qinghai: Qinghai Lake, Riyue Mountain and the rapeseed fields in flower.
By train from Qinghai to Lhasa: the Jokhang Temple and Namtso.
Yunnan: Shangri-La, Lijiang, Dali and Kunming.
Guizhou, then Guilin and Yangshuo in Guangxi.
Hunan: Mount Heng (the South) and the old town of Fenghuang; then north through Hubei.
Henan: the Shaolin Temple and Mount Song (the Centre), and Kaifeng.
Shandong: Mount Tai (the East), the last of the five.
Around the Bohai Sea through Liaoning, Hebei, Tianjin and Beijing, and back through Shanxi to Baotou.
entries.draft: From the 2013 map: the provinces are named in its caption; the way around the Bohai (a ferry from Shandong to Liaoning) and the cities are read from its line. Your text calls the 2014–15 transit your first time in Beijing: was Beijing on this loop?

entries.text: Graduated with a B.A. in English.
Moved to Shanghai for my first job.
In the two months before going abroad: Hangzhou, Wuzhen and other places around Shanghai.
Flew to Bali for my first project abroad, changing planes in Brunei without leaving the airport: Indonesia is my first country abroad.
Thirteen months in Bali, at a power plant being built on the northwest coast; I came to know nearly every corner of the island.
On Bali I learned to dive, snorkelling and then scuba, and earned a scuba certification; I also flew a paraglider and surfed for the first time.
entries.draft: Year read from context: you wrote '25'; these were before you left Bali in October 2015.

entries.text: Left Bali for nearly a week in Hong Kong.
A rest at home in Shouguang, then back to Shanghai at the end of October.
Mount Huang.
A month in Nantong, Jiangsu.
Began a part-time master's at Dalian Maritime University.
Flew to Lagos to live and work in Nigeria; home on leave about every six months.

entries.text: From Lagos, north to Niger and west to Ghana and Togo.
Doha, Qatar, for the first time.
On leave: summited the second peak of Mount Siguniang, my first snow peak; then Chengdu and Wuhan.
Doha twice more: changing planes, with time to look around each time.
Abuja, for the first time.
Beijing, properly this time; then Dubai, with Abu Dhabi, for the first time.
Istanbul, for the first time.
Completed the part-time master's (M.E. in Computer Engineering, Dalian Maritime University).
Left Nigeria through Istanbul, one last time, and went home to China.
Beijing and Shanghai, for my U.S. visa.
Left home in Shouguang at 8:08 in the morning: by road to Shanghai, then a flight to the United States.
A day in Seoul on the way.
First landing in the United States: a day in San Francisco.
On to Austin, then by taxi to San Marcos, my home for the next two years.
My first American winter and my first trip to another state: Madison, Wisconsin, then the Twin Cities.
The pandemic begins.
NASA in Houston, for the first time.
Six months living in Washington, DC.
Defended my master's at Texas State University.
Moved to Dallas to begin my Ph.D. at The University of Texas at Dallas.
Thanksgiving, my first long road trip: west to Carlsbad and White Sands, through Guadalupe Mountains and Big Bend, and home by San Antonio.
Europe, for a conference: landed in the Netherlands, by train to Cologne, then Belgium, Paris, Antwerp, Bruges, Delft, Rotterdam, The Hague and Amsterdam.

Thanksgiving in West Texas, San Antonio once more, and Wonder World park.
New Year's fireworks in Dallas.
Arkansas: hiking in Hot Springs, my first U.S. national park, and my first off-road drive; then Caddo Lake.

My first road trip driving alone, a loop: north to Salina, Kansas, west on I-70 to a conference in Denver and Rocky Mountain National Park, south to Santa Fe, and home.
